title: Gradient Boosting From Scratch
blurb: Build gradient boosting with nothing but decision trees and calculus, watch each tree fit the previous residuals, then race your version against HistGradientBoosting and LightGBM on real data.
objectives: See bias vs. variance by bootstrapping many models
Reproduce double descent with random features
Implement boosting for squared loss and log loss
Use shrinkage, subsampling and early stopping well
Benchmark against production GBDT libraries
Spot misleading feature importances
preview: Boosting stage by stage: each tree fits the shrinking residuals.

title: Trust Issues: Calibration & Conformal Prediction
blurb: Your model says 90%. Is it right 90% of the time? Diagnose overconfidence, fix it, then wrap any model in distribution-free prediction intervals and sets with guaranteed coverage.
objectives: Plot reliability diagrams and compute ECE
Fix calibration with Platt, isotonic, and temperature scaling
Implement split conformal regression intervals
Build conformalized quantile regression (CQR)
Create classification prediction sets
Check empirical coverage against the target
preview: Split conformal vs CQR bands: adaptive intervals that widen where noise grows.

title: Explain & Dethrone: SHAP vs Tabular Foundation Models
blurb: Compute exact Shapley values by brute force and check them against TreeSHAP. Then meet TabPFN, a transformer that does in-context learning on tables, and see when it beats tuned GBDTs.
objectives: Derive Shapley values by enumerating coalitions
Read beeswarm, waterfall and dependence plots
Know the correlated-feature pitfalls of SHAP
Run TabPFN in-context learning
Hold a fair GBDT vs. foundation-model showdown
preview: Boxes vs a learned prior: GBDT and TabPFN decision surfaces as the data grows.

title: Build Your Own Autograd Engine
blurb: Backprop stops being magic: write a reverse-mode autodiff engine, check it against finite differences and PyTorch, then train a neural net on it and watch the decision boundary bend.
objectives: Implement a scalar Value graph with backward()
Use topological sort to order the chain rule
Run gradient checks against finite differences
Extend the engine to numpy tensors with broadcasting
Train an MLP and match PyTorch's gradients exactly
preview: Two-moons decision boundaries learned with your own scalar and tensor autograd engines.

title: Optimizer Arena: SGD → AdamW → Muon
blurb: Implement seven optimizers as real torch.optim classes, including Muon with Newton–Schulz orthogonalization, and race them on test functions and FashionMNIST under modern LR schedules.
objectives: Write SGD, momentum, Nesterov, Adam, AdamW, Lion and Muon
See why decoupled weight decay matters
Run warmup + cosine and WSD schedules
Run an LR range test
Match torch.optim.AdamW to tolerance
preview: Seven optimizers race across Rosenbrock and Beale landscapes, with loss curves.

title: Grokking: Watching a Network Suddenly Understand
blurb: Train on modular arithmetic long after the model memorizes, then watch test accuracy jump. Find the Fourier features it discovered, and fit your own scaling law.
objectives: Reproduce delayed generalization (grokking)
Ablate weight decay and data fraction
Find the sparse Fourier structure in embeddings
Fit a power-law scaling curve
Reason about compute-optimal training
preview: Train accuracy hits 100% instantly; test accuracy jumps thousands of steps later.

title: A Modern GPT From Scratch
blurb: Build a Llama-style language model piece by piece (RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, pre-norm residuals, weight tying), train it on Shakespeare, and look inside its attention heads.
objectives: Implement causal multi-head attention and verify it against SDPA
Implement and visualize rotary position embeddings
Assemble RMSNorm + SwiGLU pre-norm blocks
Train with AdamW, warmup/cosine and clipping
Visualize attention and generate text
preview: Trained attention heads: a previous-token head and a word-start head on Shakespeare.

title: Inference Engineering: KV Cache, Sampling, Speculation & Quantization
blurb: Make generation fast and good: build a KV cache and benchmark it, write every popular sampler, prove speculative decoding is exact, and quantize weights to int8 and int4.
objectives: Implement and benchmark a KV cache
Write greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p and min-p sampling
Show that speculative decoding preserves the target distribution
Apply absmax and group-wise int8/int4 quantization
Explain the ideas behind FlashAttention and PagedAttention
preview: How top-k, top-p and min-p truncate real next-character distributions.

title: Beyond Dense Attention: Mixture-of-Experts & State-Space Models
blurb: Route tokens to experts with a load-balancing loss, then build a Mamba-style selective SSM with sequential and parallel scans and test it against attention on long-range recall.
objectives: Implement top-k routing with capacity limits
Add a load-balancing auxiliary loss
Build a selective SSM recurrence
Implement a parallel associative scan and check it
Compare attention vs. SSM on accuracy and scaling
preview: Expert utilisation: routing collapse without balancing vs aux-loss and bias balancing.

title: Flow Matching From Scratch (Noise → Art in 2D)
blurb: The core idea behind modern image and video generators, in 2D where you can see everything. Train a velocity field, integrate an ODE from noise to data, then straighten the paths with reflow.
objectives: Trace the path from VAE to diffusion to flow matching
Train conditional flow matching with linear paths
Write Euler and Heun ODE samplers
Use reflow to get good few-step sampling
Compare against DDPM noise prediction
preview: Noise particles flowing along learned trajectories into Buzz the Backprop Bee.

title: Class-Conditional Generation with Classifier-Free Guidance
blurb: Train a small conditional UNet on MNIST, add label dropout, and turn the classifier-free guidance knob to see the quality vs. diversity trade-off appear in front of you.
objectives: Build a time- and class-conditioned UNet
Train with label dropout for CFG
Sweep guidance scales and compare sample grids
Make denoising filmstrips
Understand latent diffusion and DiT at a conceptual level
preview: Same noise, guidance w = 0, 1, 2: scribbles become crisp, class-correct digits.

title: Multimodal Magic: Contrastive Learning & CLIP
blurb: Implement the InfoNCE loss and watch a tiny two-tower model align images with text, then use a pretrained CLIP for zero-shot classification, prompt ensembling and retrieval.
objectives: Implement symmetric InfoNCE (the CLIP loss)
Train a toy two-tower model
Classify zero-shot with prompt engineering
Retrieve images and text from a shared embedding space
Implement the SigLIP sigmoid loss
preview: CLIP text-to-image search: "a red car", "antlers", "a ship on the water".

title: LoRA & Friends: Fine-Tuning a Small LLM
blurb: Write LoRA from scratch, prove merge and unmerge are exact, then fine-tune SmolLM2 on your own instruction set with chat templates and prompt-token loss masking.
objectives: Implement a LoRA linear layer (A, B, α/r)
Verify merged weights are equivalent
Format data with chat templates and loss masks
Compare generations before and after fine-tuning
Know where QLoRA, DoRA and preference tuning fit
preview: A true rank-4 update vs LoRA r=1 (fails) and r=4 (matches it).

title: Teaching Models to Reason with RL (GRPO)
blurb: The 2025 reasoning recipe, hands-on: verifiable rewards, group-relative advantages, a clipped policy loss with KL. Watch the reward climb, then compare it with DPO and test-time voting.
objectives: Write reward functions for format and correctness
Implement GRPO advantages and the clipped loss
Train a policy and watch the reward rise
Implement the DPO loss
Measure best-of-N and self-consistency
preview: Test-time scaling: pass@N and majority vote, SFT policy vs GRPO policy.

title: Build an Agent: Tools, RAG & MCP
blurb: Build retrieval from scratch, write a tool-using agent loop with the Claude API (a mock LLM runs it offline), serve your tools over the Model Context Protocol, and evaluate it all.
objectives: Build and evaluate chunking, embedding and retrieval (recall@k)
Write a tool-use agent loop with traces
Write an MCP server and connect a client to it
Build a mini eval harness
Defend against prompt injection in retrieved docs
preview: Agent trace swimlane: question → retrieve → calculate → answer.

title: Peeking Inside: Sparse Autoencoders & Steering
blurb: Collect GPT-2's residual-stream activations, train a sparse autoencoder to pull out interpretable features, inspect what makes them fire, and steer generation by adding feature directions.
objectives: Use the logit lens to watch predictions form
Train a ReLU or TopK sparse autoencoder
Track L0, explained variance and dead latents
Find the top-activating tokens for each feature
Steer generation with forward hooks
preview: Logit lens: GPT-2's guess drifts England → Rome → London → Paris through the layers.
